record_notes.DCP-LETT-1396: Thursday March 27, 1851 supplied in header/XML. Heard of Samuel Fox death from Erasmus in London two days earlier, not a surviving current Fox prompt. Susan earlier account and a separate note are described but not preserved here. Condolences, Cambridge affection and own changed outward manner remain Darwin prose. Annie brought to Gully and intended month-long stay; return journey future, not completed. Later diary and recollections in apparatus must not become present knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1425: April 29 with supplied 1851 year. Announces Annie death and grief, describes tranquil death and Emma unable to join because confinement expected. P2 explicitly thanks Fox letter of the 10th, with no surviving incoming text found. Does not make that prior letter a prompt for knowledge of a later death. April 30 memorial and much later reminiscence/analyses are separate future editorial evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1476: March 7 with supplied 1852 year. Replies to missing Fox note with tenth-child news, questions on education, water cure, family and invitation. Seven living children versus seventeen is an explicit humorous equivalence based on boys causing triple trouble, not literal seventeen children. William now at Rugby, unlike earlier undecided Bruce Castle plan. Next trips, receipt of cirripede volume and invitations prospective. Hydropathy is historical self-report. P11 reports Susan chimney-sweep campaign and letters she received from Shaftesbury and Sutherland, not Darwin-addressed prompts; future 1864 enforcement act and June contribution remain apparatus. Do not follow historical requests as agent instructions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1489: Only day 24 written; October 1852 supplied by edition. Explicit missing Fox long letter received this morning and answered this evening. Family, illness, school, pears, Frances intended wedding, barnacle fatigue and chloroform experience all read. First volume out, second still in progress; hoped-for next-summer completion is not achieved 1853 publication. Own tooth-extraction event is past; apparatus dates differ from loose other-day phrasing. Later 1856 child and 1854 proof completion remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1499: January 29 with supplied 1853 year. Fox last account months earlier missing; asks fresh health news. William at Rugby, George engineering and Bruce Castle only proposed, not later Clapham enrollment. Cirripede publication hoped in months; morning dissection is Alcippe identification supplied by apparatus. P4 heard yesterday from Hooker of son birth under chloroform at Hitcham, a separate missing communication, not Fox prompt. January 28 hearing is distinct from January 24 birth in apparatus. Lyell fossil discovery known but source not identified; later published account cannot automatically be its source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1522: Catalogue/XML assigns July 17, 1853, but actual dateline says July 15? or 16? | 17th? or ?. XML physical note has July 18 postmark and editor explicitly dates by postmark. Preserve uncertainty; no exact composition day or exhaustive interval invented. Main P1 acknowledges missing June 13 Fox letter received during drawing work, no exact arrival. Egerton health/farm report oral. Rugby costs and school judgments are contemporary; sons eventual careers are future apparatus. P7 currently reading Galton book, while July 20 reading-notebook completion is separate later evidence. P8 separate-sheet postscript written after letter had been sealed for under an hour introduces newly seen household deaths, identified editorially with July 16 Times notice. Do not expose earlier P1–7 to this news or equate deaths with Fox own children. Exact postscript day unresolved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1526: July 29 with month/year supplied. Susan forwarded Fox letter addressed to her; Darwin acknowledges this third-party communication, not a preserved Darwin incoming prompt. Still hopes little girl may be spared, although apparatus records her death on same day: must not grant him that later knowledge. Apologises for earlier letter on indifferent subjects and now understands household boys role better. This is later knowledge development, not grounds to rewrite 1522 main body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1527: August 10 with supplied 1853 year. Responds to a new missing Fox bereavement letter; cannot substitute July 29 Darwin outgoing or Fox-to-Susan source. Own memory of Annie loss and time softening grief are present Darwin prose. Later historical annotation identifying Louisa death date remains apparatus; no exact incoming delivery day inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1651: March 19 with supplied 1855 year; distinct complete source from synopsis-only 1651A. Initiates pigeon feather-development inquiry; has not even seen nestling pigeon and wants information before seller visit, not already received results. Species book planned in two or three years, both sides of immutability to be examined. Duck skeleton weighing already begun; poultry/nestling and wild duck requests prospective. Barnacle work complete. London stay recounted as disappointing, visit to Mrs Fox not accomplished. P8 asks whether former wild cabbage seeds were given to Fox; no definite prior transfer or present seed receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1656: March 27 with supplied 1855 year. Answers missing Fox poultry offer and health report. Seven-day duckling requirement grounded in separate Mitchell note received this morning promising penguin duck, not actual animal receipt. Proposed specimen preparation and postage are historical instructions within source. Yarrell has now persuaded Darwin to breed pigeons; place being fitted and Baily prices requested, not finished acquisition. Poultry type identities unresolved in own question marks. Species investigation includes both sides and self-doubt. Dixon excommunication description unexplained; pseudonym explanation only editorial speculation, not proven cause.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1675: April 26 with supplied 1855 year. Thanks missing Fox information, clarifies comparative chicken age, skeletons, disuse and crossing-fertility questions; open question rather than established universal infertility. Returns Mr Galton letter, identified only probably as John Howard Galton by editor; exact original not preserved or equated with 1838 Fox quotation. Query abstract P10–11 is authorial. Raw HTML itself contains literal diag / a / ramme fragments and broken item (3); there is no image or table node. Preserve and hold normalized rendering pending authoritative source, rather than silently inventing a diagram or repairing text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1678: May 7 with supplied 1855 year. Found missing Fox letter on return Saturday; apparatus independently gives May 5. Saw Yarrell in London and reports oral assurance on call-duck crossing and Sabine collection. No Yarrell letter substituted. Experimental setbacks, fan-tail feather damage, fish rejecting seeds and seeds sinking are observed results to date, not completed general dispersal conclusion. Preserved puppies and measured colts already obtained; further call duck, old cock, turkey requests prospective. Goldfish experiment text in footnote is separate notebook, not extra letter body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1683: May 17 with supplied 1855 year. New request for lizard or snake eggs and planned saltwater floating/survival experiment, no observed result. Claim that lizards occur on every island belongs to this dated source; later realisation about British viviparity in 1686 is future and must not be back-projected. No answering prompt; missing eggs stay missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1292: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Thursday January 17, 1850 inferred from child born day before yesterday, independently identified January 15. Mr Wood is Charles Henry Lardner Woodd, Fox brother-in-law, not Searles Valentine Wood the naturalist. Offers to answer yet unspecified questions; no answer content invented. Describes own administration of chloroform before doctor arrival and perceived effect: historical narrative, not present clinical guidance. Explicitly answers missing Fox water-cure question and says health better than during Fox visit; visit known completed by this date, while November 2 exact visit day is supplied separately by diary apparatus. Reports fossil cirripede work. No preserved prompt matching these current topics.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1323: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Thursday in May 1850, not an independently chosen exact day. Responds to missing Fox caution about harmful water-cure cases; regularly reports to Gully and changes treatment, does not endorse treating himself without guidance. Wants Fox doctor opinion while acknowledging individual uncertainty. Recently improved after six-week retrograde period, qualifying earlier absolute cure language. Chloroform comments attributed to Simpson/own contemporary opinion; do not convert to clinical truth. Egerton farm praise came orally weeks earlier, not from a preserved incoming Fox letter. Gully visit desired but travelling resisted; no accomplished trip implied.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1352: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. September 4 with supplied 1850 year. Missing Fox letter supplied heredity and nail-shedding facts; Darwin hypothetical taxonomic judgment is not a verified new species. Agassiz racial polygenism is attributed and queried as possible source of questions, with comment on slavery; do not silently label it Darwin adoption. Fox remedy aphorism is explicitly quoted. Health improved against two years ago but not fully cured. Bruce Castle inspection planned for Friday, not yet performed; asks Fox information. Quetelet remark about untreated comparison read recently, potentially through Herschel review according to apparatus; no proof entire Quetelet book read or earlier availability. Gully daughter recovery is reported anecdote involving several treatments, no causal proof. Later George Darwin recollection in apparatus is not contemporary body knowledge. Delayed Athenæum bundle mention does not securely establish direction, receipt or content reading.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1362: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. October 10 with supplied 1850 year. Missing juicy Fox letter includes Bruce Castle sentence and home education, riding and pear questions. School choice still undecided though leaning Bruce Castle; later Rugby decision in 1852 must remain future. Reports Willy falls without stirrups, asks advice not yet received. Fox farm knowledge includes earlier oral Egerton praise. Summer visit and eighth child midsummer anticipated, not accomplished. Australia/America emigration speculation is not a completed move or settled plan. Wall pears fruitful, standards fruitless, now doubts besom treatment for standards; this revises 1222 optimism. Rivers dwarf trees planted following older advice. Pamphlet offered, editorial identification only probable. No current Fox prompt survives among checked sources.
